questions.text: There are two bags containing X red, 7 green, and 8 black balls together in bag 1 and 3 red, 5 green, and 7 black balls together in bag 2. If the probability of choosing a red or a green ball from bag 1 or from bag 2 is 17/30, find the value of X.
questions.explanation:
Solution:

There are two bags, so the probability of choosing a bag is 1/2.

So, the probability of choosing a red or a green ball from bag 1 = (X + 7)/(X + 15)

And the probability of choosing a red or a green ball from bag 2 = 8/15

So, the probability of choosing a red or a green ball from bag 1 or bag 2

= (1/2) (((X + 7)/(X + 15)) + (8/15))

17/15 = ((X+7)/(X + 15)) + (8/15)

9/15 = (X +7)/(X + 15)

X = 5

questions.text: A bag contains 5 red balls and some blue balls. If the probability of drawing a blue ball from the bag is four times that of a red ball, then the number of blue balls in the bag is

options.text: More than one of the above

questions.explanation:
Given:

Red balls = 5

Blue balls = m

Concept used:

Probability = Number of favorable outcomes / Number of possible outcomes

Calculation:

Probability of getting red ball = 5/(5 + m)

Probability of getting blue ball = m/(5 + m)

According to the question,

⇒ \(\dfrac{m}{m+5} = 4 \dfrac{5}{m+5}\) 

⇒ m = 20

∴ The number of blue balls are 20.

questions.text: In a school, every student offers either Hindi or English or both. 50.8% offer Hindi and 64.2% offer English. If the total number of students is 500, how many students offer both Hindi and English?

options.text: More than one of the above

questions.explanation:
Given:

Hindi = 50.8%

English = 64.2%

Total students = 500

Concept used:

n(A ⋃ B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ⋂ B)

Calculation:

Let, A = Hindi

B = English

n(A ⋃ B) = 500

n(A) = 0.508 × 500 = 254

n(B) = 0.642 × 500 = 321

⇒ 500 = 254 + 321 - n(A ∩ B)

⇒ n(A ∩ B) = 254 + 321 - 500

⇒ n(A ∩ B) = 75

∴ Number of students who opted both Hindi & English are 75.

questions.text: ​A tub contains 4 blue and 3 yellow marbles. A second tub contains 2 blue and 4 yellow marbles. One tub is selected at random. From the selected tub, one marble is drawn. Find the probability that the marble is taken out is blue.
questions.explanation:
Concept used:

Classical definition of probability.

Formula used:

Probability = Favorable Outcome / Total Outcome.

P(E) = n(E)/n(S)

Calculation:

A blue marble can be taken in two mutually exclusive ways

(i) Selecting tub I and then taking a blue marble from it.

(ii) Selecting tub II and then taking a blue marble from it.

Let E1, E2 and A denote the events defined as follows:

E1 = selecting tub I,

E2 = selecting tub II

A = taking a blue marble

Since one of the two tubs is selected randomly, therefore

P(E1) = 1/2 and P(E2) = 1/2

P(AE1) = Probability of taking a blue marble when the first tub has been selected is 4/7

P(AE2) = Probability of taking a blue marble when the second tub has been selected is 2/6

 Using the law of total probability, we have

P(blue marble) = P(A) = P(E1) × P(AE1) + P(E2) × P(AE2)

⇒ {(1/2) × (4/7)} + {(1/2) × (2/6)}

⇒ 19/42

∴ The probability that the marble taken out blue is 19/42.

questions.text: Probability that a machine receives a signal is 90%, probability that it interprets it correctly is 95% and probability of it transmitting the signal is 80%. Find the probability that a signal is received, interpreted and transmitted.
questions.explanation:
Given:-

Probability of receiving a signal = 90% = 9/10

Probability of interpreting it correctly = 95/100 = 19/20

Probability of transmitting it = 80% = 4/5

Concept:-

Probability of two or more unrelated events happening = P1 × P2 × ….. P(n)

Calculation:-

Required probability = 9/10 × 19/20 × 4/5 = 684/1000 = 171/250

questions.text: A bowl contains 16 marbles of three colors, 6 red, 4 blue and rest of purple. Three marbles are drawn one by one and not replaced. What is probability that the marbles drawn are of three different colors and first being red color?
questions.explanation:
Given:

16 marbles = 6 red + 4 blue + 6 purple

Calculation:

There are two options in this scenario

⇒ Case 1 = Red, Blue, Purple would be drawn out

⇒ Case 2 = Red, Purple, Blue would be drawn out

⇒ Probability in case 1 = (6 / 16) × (4 / 15) × (6 / 14)

⇒ Probability in case 2 = (6 / 16) × (6 / 15) × (4 / 14)

⇒ Probability = ((6 / 16) × (4 / 15) × (6 / 14)) + ((6 / 16) × (4 / 15) × (6 / 14))

⇒ Probability = 2 × (6 × 4 × 6) / (16 × 15 × 14)

⇒ Probability = 2 × 18 / 420

⇒ Probability = 3 / 35

∴ Probability of drawing out three different marbles of different colors with first being red is 3 / 35

Hint

Find probability of any one arrangement first and double it up seeing numerators and denominators remain the same

questions.text: There's a bag which contains 2 types of balls, some red and others blue. Probability of getting a blue ball is 0.3 and total number of blue balls are 15. If 20 more green balls are added to the bag what would be the probability of getting a red ball.
questions.explanation:
Given 

P(Blue ball) = 0.3

n(Blue ball) = 15

20 more green balls are added to the bag

Concept used

Total no. of balls = n(Blue ball) / P(Blue ball)

P(Red ball) =  n(Red ball) / Total balls

Calculation

Total Balls  = 15/0.3 = 50

Blue balls = 15

Red balls = 50 - 15 = 35

Now, 20 more green balls are added

Total Balls = 50 + 20 = 70

P(Red balls) = 35 / 70 = 0.5

∴ The required answer is 0.5

questions.text: When three fair dice are thrown simultaneously, what is the probability that the first die shows up an even number, the second die shows up an even prime number and the third die shows up a composite number?
questions.explanation:
Calculation:

Let A: the event of the first die showing up an even number, 2, 4, or 6.

B: the event of the second die showing up an even prime number, 2.

C: the event of the third die showing up a composite number 4 or 6.

Their respective probabilities being,

⇒ P(A) = 3/6 = 1/2, P(B) = 1/6, and P(C) = 2/6 = 1/3

The require probability is obtained by compounding these events by multiplying individual probabilities.

Hence the require probability = 1/2 × 1/6 × 1/3 = 1/36

∴ The required result will be 1/36.

questions.text: Mohan is trying to break a bulb by throwing paper balls at it. He hits the bulb 5 out of 8 times and the bulb breaks 2 out of 5 times on hitting. Find the probability of bulb breaking.
questions.explanation:
Concept used:

Classical definition of probability.

Formula used:

Probability = Favorable Outcome / Total Outcome.

Calculation:

For breaking the bulb, both the conditions must be satisfied. Mohan hitting the bulb and bulb breaking.

Probability of Mohan hitting = 5 / 8

Probability of bulb breaking on hitting = 2 / 5

Required probability = 5 / 8 × 2 / 5 = 1 / 4

questions.text: There are 5 blue, 7 green and some yellow bottles in a sack. If one bottle is drawn at random, the probability of it being yellow is 1/3. Three bottles are taken out at random, the probability of all three being different is?
questions.explanation:
GIVEN:
Blue bottles = 5

Green bottles = 7

Probability of selecting Yellow = 1/3

FORMULA USED:

P = Favorable outcomes/Total outcomes

CALCULATION:

Let there are x yellow bottles,

A.T.Q

x/(x + 12) = 1/3

⇒ 3x = x + 12

⇒ x = 6

Ways of selecting three different bottles = 5C1 × 7C1 × 6C1 = 5 × 7 × 6 = 210

Required probability = 210/18C3 = 210/816 = 35/136

∴ The probability is 35/136
